beliefs: The cubic is nearly odd: f(-x)≈-f(x) for |x|>=2.6, e.g. f(-128)≈8175362 vs -f(128)≈8181913 [E1]

There is a special interval roughly |x|<2 where f deviates strongly from the cubic and is not odd: f(1.2)≈-2.5, f(1.5)≈-5.5, f(1.9)≈-18.8 while f(-1.2)≈6.6-9.3, f(-1.5)≈11.6-14.1, f(-1.9)≈27 [E2, E3, E4]
The transition to the cubic regime happens near |x|≈2: f(2)≈-25 fits cubic, f(1.9)≈-18.8 close to cubic, but f(1.5)≈-5.5 is far from cubic [E2, E3]

The negative-side values in [0.9,1.5] are noisy and not monotone (e.g. f(-1.2)=6.61 in E4 vs 9.32 in E2, f(-0.9)=2.75 in E4 vs 3.81 in E2), so the region has substantial noise or fine structure not captured by a smooth fit [E2, E3, E4]
The exact form inside |x|<2 is not pinned down; a smooth polynomial fit gives only approximate values there [E2, E3, E4]?
notes: Kept the cubic tail and the polynomial fit for |x|<2.6 (which matched E3 well), and noted the noise in the small-|x| region rather than overfitting to E4's noisy points, since a lookup would fail on unseen probes.
